_meta.notes: Colorado has NO per-member pressroom. Verified 2026-07-25 against leg.colorado.gov: the official roster (100 seats) links each legislator to a /legislators/{slug} biography page that carries committee assignments, sponsored bills, phone and email — and no news, press or media section of any kind. leg.colorado.gov/news and /press-releases both 404. One hundred percent of Colorado legislative press output is published by the four party caucus organizations listed below. Each entry here is a CAUCUS SOURCE, not a member. Do not attribute a record from these sources to a single legislator. See attribution_warning.
_meta.attribution_warning: Measured on 239 Colorado Senate Democrats releases published 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-25: only 25 (10.5%) name any sitting legislator in the TITLE, while 236 (99.2%) name at least one in the BODY. The mean is 3.2 distinct sitting legislators named per release; just 19 of 239 (8%) name exactly one. Body mentions also routinely include members of the OTHER party as bipartisan bill sponsors. Title-prefix attribution — the strategy the 2026-05-01 recon assumed — does not work here and would misattribute roughly nine releases in ten. Treat these as caucus-authored records with a multi-member 'mentioned' relation, resolved against co_legislators_raw.json.
_meta.duplication_warning: The two Democratic caucus sites cross-post joint releases. Of 238 Senate Democrats items and 256 House Democrats items published in 2026, 68 share an identical normalized title slug after stripping the 'JOINT RELEASE:' prefix — about 28% of the Senate Democrats 2026 output. Dedup on normalized title plus published date before insert, or the same release lands twice under two different caucus sources.
_meta.collector_status: No Colorado collector exists yet. The three collection_method values below are placeholders for collectors that still need to be written. Reusing collection_method='rss' will NOT work: pipeline/collectors/rss_collector.py line 67 calls is_external_content(), which allowlists only senate.gov, house.gov and whitehouse.gov, so every Colorado caucus URL (.com / .co) would be dropped silently. Either add a per-member allowed_domains field consumed by is_external_content(), or follow the pattern in pipeline/collectors/state_legislature_collectors.py, which does not call that filter at all.
_meta.seeds_py_note: Registering this file needs a defaults row that does not assume per-member shape, e.g. {branch: legislative, jurisdiction: co, chamber: null, office_type: caucus_pressroom}. chamber is set per entry below because two caucuses sit in each chamber.
_meta.out_of_scope_silos: coloradohouserepublicans.com/notable-press (83 URLs) is third-party clippings — verified to link out to Denver Post, Colorado Politics and Reporter Herald. coloradosenaterepublicans.com category in-the-news (id 17, 14 posts) is the same thing. Both excluded per the project's original-content-only rule. coloradohouserepublicans.com/representative-videos (50 URLs) is video only.

The only press-contact-bearing .gov page in this tier is leg.colorado.gov/legislators, which publishes member inboxes rather than press staff.

pagination.note: No RSS, no JSON API. Wix. The /news listing server-renders only the newest 12 items; older pages load via JS. Discover the full archive from the dynamic-news sitemap, then fetch each detail page for title and date. The sitemap filename embeds a Wix collection GUID that can rotate, so always resolve it from /sitemap.xml rather than hardcoding it.

scrape_config.date_note: Sitemap <lastmod> is an edit timestamp, not a publish date. Verified against https://www.cohousedems.com/news/mauro%2C-hinrichsen-statement-on-aspen-acres-wildfire — lastmod 2026-07-07, body text 'July 7, 2026'. They agree on that sample but lastmod is not authoritative; parse the 'Month D, YYYY' string from the detail page body and fall back to lastmod with lowered date_confidence.

members.notes: Highest-volume Colorado legislative source. 256 sitemap entries carry a 2026 lastmod. Lowest confidence of the four because it is the only one with no machine-readable feed and because published dates must come from detail-page text.

pagination.note: Squarespace. ?format=rss returns the newest 20 items and is enough for the daily run. ?format=json returns the same 20 with a millisecond publishOn timestamp; pass the last item's publishOn as &offset to walk back. Verified: 141 items retrieved in 8 requests, oldest 2023-07-06.

scrape_config.date_note: publishOn is epoch milliseconds UTC. Authoritative; date_confidence 1.0.

members.notes: Very low current volume: 9 items in 2026 and nothing newer than 2026-05-12 as of 2026-07-25. That is a real editorial pattern for a minority caucus out of session, not a broken collector — do not let a stale-source alert fire on this one without a long threshold. Set expected cadence to roughly monthly.
